text:
sana: rolled the 8-bit PTQ reranker to a 1% canary. offline ndcg ~+0.3% but saw a small dip in click-through on the canary. dashboard: https://rbwd/metrics/rc-1pct

adi: did we change candidates?

sana: no, only quantized weights. command used: `quantize --model rerank-3 --bits 8 --scheme symmetric`

maria: historical note: average ndcg can mask head-query top1 flips that affect CTR. please run a head/mid/tail breakdown with top1_precision and swap_rate.

adi: running eval now: `eval --model rerank-3-8bit --slices freq:head,freq:mid,freq:tail --metrics ndcg,mrr,top1_precision,swap_rate --topk 5`

bench-bot: job 1761112350 queued (est 3h)

sana: sampled some prod traces: saw multiple queries where top1 swapped after quantization by tiny margins (0.0005-0.002).

maria: that small margin is classic quant granularity. what tie-breaker do we use?

adi: fallback is candidate_id lexical. could be arbitrary.

sana: quick local probe: keep final logits in fp16 and quantize rest -> top1_precision head improved from -2.1% to -0.4% in sample of 1000 head queries.

maria: good evidence for hybrid precision for logits. also we should log order_hash + score_bucket for a small percent of production to repro.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: auto-rollback scheduled if CTR delta < -1.5% over 1h on canary group rc-1pct.

maria: plan: 1) wait for bench job, 2) run a tiny QAT (pairwise hinge loss focused on top1) on head subset, 3) instrument prod logging for order_hash. avoid heuristic offsets to scores.

sana: agreed. will pause canary expansion and post artifacts when bench completes. /cc @eng-sre
